card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the missing cake taken, dropped, or eaten by the dog? Describe the crumbs before choosing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. Were those crumbs present before dinner too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, after you fed it your slice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then theft returns to contention. Start again with who opened the cupboard.

The pair originated with D126-a's 0.25.0 instruction to build the object before the story; revised D126-a instead tests fabric versus cardboard and whether one container was inside another. Those parcel specifics are not in this cake scene; the detail-first method remains its contribution. This is an explicit provenance amendment, not a new semantic pair review. Exact pair review remains pending.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The parcel was lost, stolen, or delivered elsewhere. Was it a bag or a box?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A box with handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delivery error leads. Describe the lid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was tied, not hinged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'box' loses support. Let's establish the container before accusing a driver.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Adapts S144-single-b's competing explanations and changing preference to a missing parcel, using D126-single-a's bag-versus-box, handles and lid inquiry. A1 proposes loss, theft and misdelivery; A3 favors delivery error after B2 describes handles, while A5 uses B4's tied lid to reconsider the container label. Originally inherited from D126-a's 0.25.0 snapshot, the bag/box, handle and lid inquiry survives the revised seed; the revised fabric/cardboard and nested-container questions are not spoken here. The last pair change concerns classification, not a demonstrated switch among the original disappearance theories. card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake's gone: theft, accident, or the dog. I suspect theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on him. Get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take him; check under the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That icing's from yesterday. The crumbs lead into the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Theft leads again. Keep the dog here; let's see whether that trail ends at a dropped cake or somebody's coat.

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the parcel in a bag or a box? You've used both words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before choosing the noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had a rigid lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let's build the object before the story.

card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall lights failed: weather, wiring, or the caretaker saving electricity. Wiring's my favourite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged them. Help me reach the socket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Economy takes the lead. I'll hold your ladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The socket's wet. There's rain coming through the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather overtakes him. Leave the plug; let's ask whether he unplugged it before the leak.

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For this missing-parcel form: was it a bag or a box? You've said both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think. I carried it by the handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles. Were they attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. It had a rigid lid, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'bag'? Tell me again what you carried. Was the box inside something?

card.title: What Really Happened?
card.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're claiming for your lost bag. At four, were you on the bus or buying coffee? You've told me both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Coffee. Can we finish the form?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the bag beside you when you paid?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. The driver waited while I ran in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So both fit. Tell me the boarding bit again: did the bag come back out with you?
